newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BLACKBURN DENY ERIKSSON BACKING OUT OF AGREEMENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLACKBURN DENY ERIKSSON BACKING OUT OF AGREEMENT.

text.p: English premier league club Blackburn on Friday denied reports Swedish coach Sven-Goran Eriksson had asked to be released from his agreement to become manager of the club later this year.

Italian newspapers had said Eriksson, currently coach at Sampdoria, wanted to pull out of the deal after receiving a three billion lire ($1.9 million) offer to become manager at Lazio. The reports said Blackburn had agreed to his request.

But this was strongly refuted by Blackburn chairman Robert Coar. "We have a written agreement with Sven-Goran Eriksson that he'll be with us in July. That's the situation, pure and simple. There are no get-out clauses and he'll be with us in July," he said.

According to the Rome daily La Repubblica, Eriksson made his request after being asked to take over at Lazio, the serie A club which sacked Zdenek Zeman as manager on Monday and appointed former Italy goalkeeper Dino Zoff as a temporary replacement until the end of the season.

La Repubblica said Blackburn had agreed to release the 48-year-old Eriksson on condition they could find an adequate replacement and it suggested Blackburn had Inter's English coach Roy Hodgson and Barcelona's former England manager Bobby Robson in their sights.
Blackburn, premier league champions in 1995 but currently fourth from the foot of the table, signed a preliminary agreement with Eriksson in December for him to take over in July.

A front-page article in Rome's sports daily Corriere dello Sport said Eriksson's mind was definitely made-up. "Sorry, but I don't want to leave Italy any more," Eriksson was quoted as telling Blackburn, beneath the headline "Eriksson: Lazio, Si".
Eriksson enjoyed a highly successful three-year spell in the Italian capital with Lazio's arch-rivals Roma in the mid-1980s, narrowly missing out on the league title in 1986.

After periods with Fiorentina and Portugal's Benfica, Eriksson has spent the past five seasons successfully rebuilding Sampdoria, this season leading the side to second-place in the Italian first division behind Juventus.
